transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you and what brings you in to see me today?

I'm visiting today because I've been struggling with constant, uncontrollable worry about almost everything in my life, including my work, family, and money. This has been happening nearly every day for the past seven months, and I just can't seem to stop it.
Beyond the worry, have you also been feeling a persistent sense of sadness, or have you lost interest and pleasure in the activities you usually enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I feel sad or that I've lost interest in the things I usually enjoy. My main issue is really just this constant, overwhelming worry and physical tension that I can't seem to shake. It feels much more like my mind is constantly racing and anxious rather than depressed.
Since you mentioned physical tension, have you also been experiencing other physical symptoms like difficulty falling or staying asleep, feeling restless, or muscle aches?

I definitely feel incredibly restless, almost like I'm wound up like a spring and just can't sit still. My entire body constantly feels stiff and tense, making it really hard to relax. I'm not quite sure about my sleep, but this physical tension and restlessness are definitely there all the time.
Does this constant worry and physical tension make it difficult for you to carry out your daily responsibilities at work or in your personal life?

Yes, it definitely interferes with my daily life quite a bit. I find it extremely difficult to focus on my tasks at work because these anxious thoughts keep popping up, scattering my attention. Even simple personal responsibilities at home have started to feel completely overwhelming to manage.
Did these difficulties with focus and restlessness begin only within the last seven months, or have you struggled with similar challenges regarding attention and organization since you were a child?

No, I never struggled with attention or organization when I was a child; this is all a relatively recent development. These difficulties with focus and restlessness only started about seven months ago when the constant worrying began.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports excessive, uncontrollable worry about multiple domains for seven months, accompanied by physical symptoms like restlessness and muscle tension. The symptoms are not better explained by a mood disorder or childhood-onset attentional issues, and they significantly impair daily functioning.
